m: The {Dentist} sits on the {Front Step} of the {Hut}, pulling a tooth from a *white dove*. She drops it into a *ladle* and labels it: tooth **of** dove. Soon the step is lined with ladles **of** everything: the beak **of** a duck, the honk **of** a goose, the hiccup **of** a frog.

The {Yogi} meditates on the {Rooftop} of the {Beach} café, balanced on **one** *plank* on **one** toe. A seagull lands and the plank wobbles. The yogi raises **one** finger, and the whole beach freezes, holding its breath, until a single grain of sand falls and he topples into the sea.

The {Sheriff} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Beehive} and stamps every bee with a giant *tick mark*. 'You **are** a bee. You **are** a bee.' One bee insists it wants **to be** a wasp; the sheriff slaps another tick on its back, and now it simply **is**, forever, officially, a bee.

The {Baker} plunges through the {Trapdoor} into the {Pool}, waving a dripping *no sign* at everyone. Swimmers? **Not** allowed. Inflatable ducks? **Not** today. When the water tries to splash, he slaps the sign on it too, and the pool sits perfectly still, **not** moving, **not** even rippling.

The {Lifeguard} rocks a *swaddled baby* on the {Front Step} of the {Hut}, blowing her whistle as a lullaby. The baby burps, yawns and holds up a tiny sign: **done**. Feeding **done**, burping **done**, nap **done**. The lifeguard crosses off the whole day and goes home at eleven in the morning.

The {Zookeeper} falls through the {Trapdoor} of the {Island} lighthouse and lands on a huge map pinned down by a giant *left hand*. 'You **are at** this spot,' it booms, tapping a red dot. Every lost penguin waddles up, touches the hand and finally knows where it **is at**: right here.

The {Robot} clanks up the {Staircase} of the {Funfair} and builds a *person* out of candyfloss and hot-dog sticks. It sets the **person** walking on two stiff legs. The candyfloss **person** buys a ticket for the dodgems, and the robot, jealous, tries to become a **person** too by eating a toffee apple.

The {Yogi} sits cross-legged in the {Basement} of the {Boathouse}, *holding meat*: a huge ham in each hand. Hungry ducks paddle in shouting 'I want to **have** it!' The yogi smiles, grows more arms, and soon he **has** twelve hams, sixty sausages and an angry goose. To **have** is easy.

The {Wizard} hides in the {Basement} of the {Fort} while a *spearman* stomps about asking who stole the cannon. The wizard leaps out, jabs a thumb at his own chest and shouts '**I** did! **I**, me, myself!' The spearman pokes him in the belly button, but the wizard keeps pointing at himself, glowing with pride.

The {Tailor} is measuring a *standing person* on the {Rooftop} of the {Spa} when a *scorpion* scuttles out of the man's sleeve. 'Not me, **he** did it!' squeaks the scorpion. Everyone turns and points at the man: **he** ate the cucumber slices, **he** flooded the hot tub. The poor man just stands there being **he**.

The {Jockey} gallops a horse down a *road* and straight through the {Trapdoor} of the {Hut}. He skids to a stop, rolls up his sleeve and shows off a fresh *tattoo*. '**This**! Look at **this**!' he yells, jabbing at it. The tattoo shows a tiny finger jabbing right back at him: **this** one, right here.

The {Gardener} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Hut} with a *pole* and a *person* to count. She counts them **one** by **one**: **one** person, **one** pole, **one** lost sock. Everything she touches gets a little numbered flag stuck on top, until the whole room bristles with flags, each item counted as **one**.

The {Magician} taps his wand on the {Front Step} of the {Funfair} and a *standing person* walks out of the *gate*. Tap: two people. Tap: forty. Tap: a whole marching band of copies. 'One is boring,' he shouts, 'I want **plural**!' The step bulges with **plurals**, each one wearing a hat with an -s on it.

The {Jockey} stands on the {Rooftop} of the {Lagoon} lighthouse firing arrows at a *bullseye* floating on the water. Every arrow thunks into the exact **middle**. Fish swim to the **middle** to watch, boats steer to the **middle**, and the whole lagoon slowly squeezes into the **middle** until the edges are completely empty.

The {Lifeguard} blows her whistle at the top of the {Staircase} of the {Island} hotel: '**Come** here!' Up the stairs **come** sheaves of *barley*, marching on their stalks, hundreds of them, rustling and bumping. They **come** faster than she can count and bury her in a golden, sneezy pile on the landing.

The {Sheriff} bursts out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Hangar} and stomps *upstairs*, swinging his lasso. Everything follows him **up**: aeroplanes float **up**, mechanics drift **up**, a toolbox rises like a balloon. By lunch the whole hangar is stuck to the ceiling, and the sheriff is shouting '**Up**!' through a megaphone.

The {Dentist} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Spa} and lands on a *big man* soaking in the mud bath. He opens his mouth: it is **big**, so **big** that the dentist climbs inside with a torch and a ladder. Her echo booms out. The man stretches, yawns and knocks down both walls of the spa.

The {Wizard} tumbles through the {Trapdoor} of the {Lake} pier into a canoe paddled by an *elephant handler*. 'Who is this canoe **for**?' asks the wizard. 'It is **for** the elephant!' The elephant climbs in, the canoe sinks, and the handler waves a ticket: the whole lake is booked **for** one elephant.

The {Hunter} runs up the {Staircase} of the {Hut} with a *grain stalk* in one hand **and** a giant *mouth* in the other. He feeds the stalk to the mouth, **and** the mouth chews, **and** burps, **and** asks for another. Every step he climbs adds another **and**, until the stairs are piled with them.

The {Gardener} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Warehouse} and builds a *fence* around a shining *jade gem* on the landing. She plants a flag and declares a new **country**. An anthem blares from a crate, and soon the tiny **country** has stamps, a parliament of mice and a border dispute with the broom cupboard.

The {Dentist} falls through the {Trapdoor} of the {Beach} shack and hits the **ground** face first. She spits out *soil* and finds a *scorpion* tunnelling beside her. Together they drill into the **ground** with her dental drill, deeper and deeper, until the sand above sinks into a giant hole.

The {Dentist} waits by the {Trapdoor} of the {Tower} under a flashing *arrival* board. It clicks: her patient will **arrive** now! A hot-air balloon crashes through, then a horse, then a rowing boat, all shouting 'We have **arrived**!' The patient comes last, on a pogo stick, three hours late.

The {Yogi} sits in the {Basement} of the {Beach} house with one enormous *tool*. He **uses** it to open coconuts, then to comb his beard, then to paddle out to sea. Neighbours queue down the steps, all desperate **to use** it, until the tool overheats, hums angrily and starts using them instead.

The {Sheriff} climbs onto the {Rooftop} of the {Warehouse} and tries **to speak**, but only a *small speech bubble* pops out, squeaking 'hi'. A *money changer* rushes over and swaps it for a huge one. Now when the sheriff **speaks**, bubbles as big as lorries float over the town, bumping chimneys and blocking the sun.

The {Sheriff} gallops up the {Staircase} of the {Beehive} with the *sun* under one arm and a gigantic *thumb* for a clock hand. He jams the thumb into the sun and spins it: dawn, noon, sunset in three seconds. Bees check their wristwatches in panic. '**Time** is up!' he hollers, and **time** runs backwards to breakfast.

The {Yogi} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Tower} into a *cabinet* stuffed with sweets. A *woman* is already inside, munching. 'I **want** that one,' says the yogi. 'I **want** them all,' says she. They yank out drawer after drawer until the cabinet tips over and rolls down the tower, still full of wanting.

The {Juggler} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Youth Hostel} into a cardboard *palace*. First he juggles a *wart* off his own nose, **then** the palace towers, **then** the guards, **then** the queen, who keeps shouting 'And **then**?' Every catch happens instantly, no waiting at all.

The {Chef} is on the {Rooftop} of the {Pool} building when a *double mountain* bursts up through the water, one peak stacked on another. Everything **goes out**: swimmers leap **out**, inflatables fly **out**, the chef's soufflé pops **out** of the oven. The mountain shoves itself **out** through the roof and keeps growing.

The {Hunter} falls through the {Trapdoor} of the {Waiting Room} into a *meeting* of rabbits. Each rabbit stands and lists what it **can** do: juggle, yodel, knit a scarf with its ears. The hunter, embarrassed, shows that he **can** whistle. The rabbits vote that he **can** stay, if he makes the tea.

The {King} sits in the {Basement} of the {Hut} asking a *nodding head* in a jar for permission. '**Can** I eat cake for dinner?' Nod. 'Wear my crown in the bath?' Nod. '**Can** I ban Tuesdays?' The head nods so hard it rolls out of the jar and bounces up the stairs, still nodding yes.

The {Yogi} is stretching in the {Basement} of the {Hut} when a *scorpion* copies his pose. He lifts a leg; the scorpion lifts one **also**. He stands on his head; the scorpion does **also**. He sneezes, and the scorpion sneezes **also**, and so do the spiders, the mice and the boiler.

The {Ninja} creeps through the {Basement} of the {Beach} house and finds a mirror with *you* painted on it. Every time she moves, the mirror shouts '**You**!' and points. She hides in a bucket of sand: '**You**!' She disguises herself as a deckchair: '**You**, the deckchair!' There is no escaping **you**.

The {Dentist} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Waiting Room} between two *dance partners* doing a terrible tango. She grabs a clipboard: left foot **correct**, right foot wrong. She prods them with a dental mirror until every step is **correct**, and all the waiting patients stand up and cheer.

The {Sheriff} stands on the {Rooftop} of the {Jungle} treehouse and plants a single *seedling* in his hat. It starts to **grow**: through the crown, past his nose, up into the clouds. Monkeys climb it, a parrot nests in it, and the sheriff clings to the brim as he **grows** too, stretched upward like toffee.

The {Ninja} sneaks up the {Staircase} of the {Jungle} temple behind a huge *bear*. The bear spins round and shows off everything it **can** do: backflips, karate chops, silent tiptoeing. The ninja tries every move and falls over. The bear pats her head: 'Practise, and one day you **can** too.'

The {Ghost} floats up the {Staircase} of the {Car Park} dragging an enormous *beard* that snags on every step. He is a ghost, **and yet** he trips. He is invisible, **and yet** the beard is bright orange. Drivers swerve and honk, **and yet** the ghost keeps climbing, tutting at his chin.

The {Zookeeper} sits on the {Front Step} of the {Beehive} rocking a *child* dressed as a bee. The **child** buzzes, the bees buzz back, and hundreds of them swarm out to babysit. The zookeeper sneaks off for a cup of tea while the **child** conducts the whole hive like an orchestra.

The {Ninja} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Spa}, and a giant *pointing finger* swings round across the room. '**That**!' it booms. **That** towel. **That** cucumber. **That** man in the mud bath. The ninja rolls behind a potted plant, and the finger points at **that** too.

The {Dentist} sprints up the {Staircase} of the {Hut} following *footsteps* painted in glitter. At the top a *found coin* glows on the carpet. She dives **to get** it, but a pigeon **gets** there first. She chases it round and round the banisters until she **gets** the coin back, plus a feather.

The {Yogi} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Museum} and hangs himself on a *coat stand* in the hall. Visitors stare **at** him: a yogi **at** the museum, labelled like an exhibit. He stays exactly **at** that spot for three days, upside down, while schoolchildren sketch him.

The {Jockey} sits on the {Front Step} of the {Hut} watching a *sheep* with one giant *eye*. The sheep is knitting, still knitting, knitting all night, needles clicking non-stop. The jockey keeps staring, staring, and the eye stares back. Nothing ever finishes: everything is **-ing**, **ongoing** forever.

The {Shepherd} falls through the {Trapdoor} of the {Piazza} and keeps going **down** the *downstairs*: past the cellar, past the sewers, past a snoring dragon. Her sheep tumble **down** after her, bleating, one bouncing step at a time, until they all land in a woolly heap at the very bottom.

The {Zookeeper} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Beehive} and lands *nose* to nose with her own reflection in a pool of honey. She taps her nose, the way people point to mean me, my **self**. The honey taps back. Delighted, she hugs her own **self**, then buys her **self** a jar.

The {Jockey} rides a *winding path* that curls up onto the {Rooftop} of the {Beehive}. At every bend hangs a sign: Queen **of** the Bees, Honey **of** the Hive, Hat **of** the Jockey. The path coils round and round, linking everything to everything else in one long chain **of** ofs.

The {Ninja} sprints up the {Staircase} of the {Yen Exchange} in a *slanted cap*, and each step flips the calendar on by one **year**. A pair of *mirror feet* race behind her, copying every stride. By the top she has a long white beard, and the clerk hands her a cake: one hundred **years** of service.

The {Gardener} falls through the {Trapdoor} of the {Warehouse} onto a *road* where a giant *thumb* is hitchhiking. Lorries **pass**, bikes **pass**, a marching band **passes**. Nobody stops. So the gardener gives the thumb a lift in her wheelbarrow, and they **pass** everyone, overtaking a snail with a roar.

The {Firefighter} stands on the {Rooftop} of the {Spa} beside a *launch pad*, loading bathrobes and rubber ducks into a cannon. Three, two, one! She **sends out** towels, flannels and cucumber slices, all whistling across the sky. Fluffy slippers rain on the town below as she keeps **sending** more **out**.

The {Hunter} falls through the {Trapdoor} of the {Boathouse} and hides behind a *leaning cliff*. A *covered mouth* mumbles behind its hand: 'Wait until **after**.' **After** the boats leave, **after** the ducks sleep, **after** the moon sets. He waits so long he comes out a week **after** everyone forgot him.

The {Zookeeper} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Warehouse}, where a *standing person* is packing a *jack-in-the-box*. Every time the lid shuts, the jack springs out yelling 'Things **to do**!' and hands out chores. The zookeeper **does** them all: stacks crates, polishes forklifts, and finally sits on the lid.

The {Lifeguard} jumps into the {Basement} of the {Beach} hotel and finds a whole tiny *village* **inside**: cottages, a church, a duck pond. She blows her whistle and the villagers scurry **inside** their houses. She peeks **inside** one cottage and sees an even smaller village **inside** that.

The {Yogi} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Lagoon} jetty clutching a *bucket*, and finds a hundred jobs for it. He **uses** it as a hat, a drum, a boat, a bath for a crab. When a whale surfaces asking to borrow it, the yogi shows it how **to use** the bucket as a very small snorkel.

The {Dentist} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Tower} onto a *road* painted with arrows, where a giant *head* lies across it, blocking the **way**. 'Which **way** to the exit?' she asks. The head rolls its eyes left, then right, then rolls itself down the road to show her the **way**, flattening a hedge.

The {Shepherd} leads his flock up the {Staircase} of the {Boxing Ring}, where the canvas is painted as a *crossroads*. The sheep **walk** north, **walk** south, **walk** in circles, bumping into the referee. The boxers give up fighting and **walk** along behind them, and soon the whole crowd is marching round and round the ring.

The {Sailor} is down in the {Basement} of the {Warehouse}, where an *old door* stands alone in the middle of nowhere. She chops it open with an *axe*, and behind it is a secret **place**: a cosy room with a fire and slippers. She claims the **place**, hangs up her hammock and refuses ever to leave her new **place**.

The {Robot} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Mansion} with *flames* shooting out of its toaster belly. The carpet catches, **so** the curtains catch, **so** the butler grabs a hose, **so** the robot fizzes and steams, **so** everyone goes outside to toast marshmallows. One thing leads to another, and it all turns out just **so**.

The {Juggler} stands on the {Rooftop} of the {Piazza} juggling a tiny *home*, a little house with smoke curling from its chimney. Pigeons fly down and move in. A cat follows, then a grandmother with soup. Soon the whole square wants to live in the flying **home**, and he can't stop juggling, because it's everyone's **home** now.

The {Jockey} sorts seeds in the {Basement} of the {Lagoon} aquarium, flinging each *grain stalk* at a *bullseye* chart on the wall. Every **kind** lands in its own ring: rice here, wheat there, corn dead centre. A curious fish swims up demanding to know what **kind** it is, and gets flung at the chart too.

The {Sheriff} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Beehive} and dangles a *fish hook* into the honey, fishing for clues. Up comes a soggy note marked serious **matter**. The bees crowd round: 'What's the **matter**?' Someone stole the queen's crown! The sheriff hooks the culprit, a sticky wasp, and the **matter** is closed.

The {Chef} sprints up the {Staircase} of the {Jungle} temple, grabs the golden *trophy* at the top and holds it high. At once she starts **to become** someone else: her hat **becomes** a crown, her apron a cape, her spatula a sceptre. Then a monkey snatches the trophy and **becomes** king of the jungle instead.

The {Firefighter} stands on the {Rooftop} of the {Hangar} on a giant compass painted as a *square*, one **direction** on each side. She sprays her hose north, then east, then south, then west. The planes below spin to face each **direction** she points, until they are dizzy and facing every **direction** at once.

The {Dentist} climbs onto the {Rooftop} of the {Warehouse} at night and sees *many moons* rising, stacked one on another. Two, then ten, then **many** more, so **many** that the sky gets crowded and they start bumping. She tries to count them with her little mirror, gives up, and writes **many** on her clipboard.

The {Juggler} stands on the {Rooftop} of the {Boxing Ring} threading a long *silk thread* through a needle the size of a canoe. The thread must **pass through** everything: the ropes, the referee's ear, both boxers' gloves, the popcorn machine. By sunset the whole arena is stitched together, the thread having **passed through** it all.

The {Magician} sits on the {Front Step} of the {Hut} and pulls a *tiny thread* from his sleeve. It keeps coming: ten metres, a hundred, a kilometre. Neighbours gather, scratching their heads. '**What**?' says one. '**What**?!' says another. The thread finally ends in a small pink rabbit, which looks around and also says '**What**?'

The {Cheerleader} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Museum}, waving pompoms at a glowing *exit* sign. 'Let's **go**! **Go**, **go**, **go**!' The dinosaur skeletons get up and clatter out the door. The mummies follow, then the paintings, then the guards, all chanting, until the museum is empty and everything has **gone**.

The {Firefighter} is stuck in the {Basement} of the {Spa} and needs a **method** to get out. Plan one, shouting, fails. Plan two: she cries so many *water drops* that the room floods and she floats up through the *exit* like a cork. She writes it down as the perfect **method** and teaches it to the goldfish.

The {Shepherd} sits on the {Staircase} of the {Ice Rink} teaching a *child* to skate from a fat textbook. The child **studies** chapter one and falls over. **Studies** chapter two and spins into a wall. By chapter nine she is doing triple jumps while reading, and the shepherd is the one who needs **to study**.

The {Robot} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Pool} diving board and shouts 'What **if** I jump?' The *echo* answers: '**If** I jump... **if** I jump...' The robot freezes. What **if** it rusts? What **if** it sinks? The echo keeps asking, and the robot stands there for an hour, metal toes curled over the edge.

The {Dentist} lands on the {Rooftop} of the {Boathouse} and sees a whole *capital city* floating down the river: palaces, trams, a parliament. She decides to check **all** its teeth. **All** the citizens queue up, **all** the statues open wide, even the trams. By midnight she has polished **all** of them until the city sparkles.

The {Tailor} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Lagoon} villa sewing outfits that are all the **same**. Everyone gets the **same** striped suit and drinks from *matching cups*. Even the flamingos wear them. When a crab turns up in a different hat, the tailor faints, wakes, and quickly makes it the **same** too.

The {Shepherd} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Yen Exchange}, where a *king* and a *watcher* stare at a giant clock. 'When can we swap money?' asks the king. '**Now**!' shouts the watcher. 'Right **now**?' '**Now**!' The coins leap out of the tills that instant, and the shepherd is buried in yen before anyone can blink.

The {Dentist} is on the {Rooftop} of the {Hangar} when a plane's brakes fail. There is no barrier, so she leaps down **to act as** a *roadblock*. Next she has **to act as** the pilot, then the control tower, waving a torch. By nightfall she is **acting as** the entire airport, wearing six hats at once.

The {Magician} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Lake} lighthouse waving a *war club* like a wand. *Water drops* splash everywhere as his things vanish: hat gone, rabbit gone, trousers gone. He pats his pockets. He does **not have** a coin. He does **not have** a sock. He does **not have** anything at all, except the club.

The {Dentist} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Lagoon} jetty onto a *cloud* that won't budge. A *strong arm* rises from the water and shoves it. Now everything starts **to move**: the cloud drifts, the island slides, the palm trees jog. Nothing stays still, and the dentist **moves** round the lagoon at fifty miles an hour.

The {Magician} pops up through the {Trapdoor} of the {Yen Exchange} and pulls a giant rubber *face* out of his hat. He slaps it onto the cashier's window, and now the window has a **face** that winks at customers. He pulls out more and more, until every coin and banknote has a grinning little **face**.

The {Cheerleader} is in the {Basement} of the {Beach} house when a *runner* trips over a *coiled rope*. The rope springs alive and shoots straight up like a charmed snake. Everything starts **to rise**: the runner, the cheerleader, a sofa, a sleepy crab. They all **rise** through the ceiling and keep **rising** into the sky.

The {King} climbs out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Mansion} with a *shading hand* above one enormous *eye*. He **looks** left, he **looks** right, scanning the ballroom like a sailor at sea. '**Look**! Land ho!' he shouts, pointing at the buffet. All the guests **look** too, hands at their brows, squinting at the sandwiches.

The {Dentist} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Boxing Ring} onto a *roof* that keeps sliding about. She slams down a *foot stop* and the roof is **fixed**, stuck fast. Then she **fixes** the referee in place, **fixes** the bell, **fixes** both boxers mid-punch. Nothing can wobble now: the whole fight is frozen like a photo.

The {Tailor} sits on the {Rooftop} of the {Yen Exchange} sewing the *sky* like a big blue blanket. She stitches in the sun and it is **day**. She unpicks it and it is night. Stitch: **day**. Unpick: night. The clerks below keep opening and shutting the shop, and by lunch they have had forty **days**.

The {Firefighter} balances on the {Rooftop} of the {Funfair} with a huge *cut cake* and an axe. Hungry children below scream for a slice. She **divides** it in half, then quarters, then hundreds of crumbs, flinging them down like confetti. Still they want more, so she starts **to divide** the crumbs as well.

The {Hunter} trudges up the {Staircase} of the {Island} temple along a *road* with a *no sign* on every step. He is tired, he is soaked, and he is **still** climbing. A storm blows the signs over; he is **still** climbing. Hours later he reaches the top, and the last sign **still** says no.

The {Juggler} falls through the {Trapdoor} of the {Inn} into a *well* beside the *road*. A sign at the bottom says **Enter**. She **enters** a door in the wall, then another, each one smaller, until she squeezes in and **enters** a tiny room where the innkeeper is serving soup to mice.

The {Hunter} tiptoes into the {Basement} of the {Tower}, where a *woman* hugs her *child* and hands out gold stars. Everything she touches turns **good**: mouldy bread goes fresh, bats sing in harmony, his muddy boots shine. '**Good**,' she nods at him. '**Good** boy.' He blushes and puts down his bow.

The {Shepherd} sneaks into the {Basement} of the {Cat Café} and scatters *crumbs* everywhere. Every cat that eats one shrinks: **small**, smaller, as tiny as a thimble. Soon he is herding a flock of **small** kittens with a toothpick. The owner hunts for her cats and finds them in a teacup, purring in very **small** voices.

The {Baker} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Pool} onto a *hillside* made of jelly. A *spitting mouth* at the top spits out **parts**: a wheel, a pedal, a bell, a saddle. The baker bolts each **part** to the next and builds a wobbly bicycle, then rides it straight down the hill and into the deep end.

The {Cheerleader} bounces up the {Staircase} of the {Beach} tower tossing grain in a *winnowing basket*. Every grain flies home to **its** own spot, every shell to **its** own crab, every crab to **its** own rock. The basket hops back to **its** own hook, and she yells, 'Everything in **its** place!'

The {Shepherd} stands on the {Rooftop} of the {Yeti Cave}, on *this spot* laid across *two planks*, handing out snacks. 'Want **some**?' The yeti takes **some** biscuits. A goat takes **some** cheese. Then the planks creak, and **some** of the snacks slide off, landing on **some** very surprised skiers below.

The {Jockey} sits in the {Basement} of the {Pool} holding one tall *candle*, the only light. Whoever holds the candle is the **master**. The cleaners bow, the inflatable flamingos salute, the drain gurgles 'Yes, **master**.' Then a frog snatches the candle and becomes **master**, ordering everyone to croak.

The {Yogi} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Hangar} into a fashion show where a *tree* and a *sheep* swap outfits. The tree in the woolly coat looks like a sheep; the sheep in leaves looks like a bush. The judges score only **appearance**, so the yogi changes his **appearance** too, dressing as a jet plane.

The {Lifeguard} is called down to the {Basement} of the {Beach} hotel, where a *king* is about to sell his whole *village* for a lollipop. 'What's your **reason**?' she demands. He has no **reason**. She makes him write one **reason** after another on a whiteboard until he sighs and keeps the village.

The {Shepherd} sits on the {Rooftop} of the {Inn} holding a giant *heart* that thumps like a drum. Every beat pulses through the building: beds bounce, soup sloshes, the guests' own **hearts** thump in time. The shepherd hands the **heart** to a lonely sheep, which falls instantly in love with the chimney.

The {Tailor} stitches a ballgown on the {Rooftop} of the {Spa} for a *woman* with a pet *scorpion* on her shoulder. '**She** wants sequins,' the scorpion clicks. '**She** wants feathers. **She** wants a cape.' The woman just nods. The scorpion does all the talking, and it is always **she** this, **she** that.

The {Baker} goes down to the {Basement} of the {Funfair} and finds the whole place held up by *roots*. She tugs one **root** and the carousel above spins. She tugs another and the Ferris wheel wobbles. Everything grows from this one tangle, so she digs to the very **root** and finds a carrot running the fair.

The {Cheerleader} cartwheels up the {Staircase} of the {Yen Exchange} straight to the *front* of the queue. Everyone else is behind her, grumbling. 'I'm in **front**!' she shouts, bouncing off a counter and landing in **front** of the manager. He hands her every coin just to get her out by the **front** door.

The {King} sits on the {Rooftop} of the {Island} castle and lifts a heavy *door bar*, and everything bursts **open**: windows, cupboards, treasure chests, clams on the beach, even the clouds. Coconuts **open** and squirt milk. The king laughs, and his mouth swings so wide **open** that a seagull flies in.

The {Dentist} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Mansion} beside a *standing person* waiting for the *sunrise*. 'Here it comes!' **But** the curtains are shut. He opens them. **But** it's raining. The rain stops. **But** it's only a painting of a sunrise. The dentist yawns: 'Yes, **but** it's three in the morning.'

The {Yogi} unrolls a *sleeping mat* on the {Rooftop} of the {Inn} and snores so loudly the tiles shake. That snore is the **cause** of everything: windows rattle, guests fall out of bed, cows stampede in the field. The innkeeper follows the chaos back up the stairs and finds the **cause**, still snoring.

The {Jockey} goes down to the {Basement} of the {Beehive} and finds a *lone bird* sitting on one egg. It is the **only** bird there, with the **only** egg, in the **only** nest, surrounded by a million buzzing bees. The jockey offers to babysit, but the bird shakes its head: **only** me.

The {Tsar} sweeps down the {Staircase} of the {Lagoon} palace with a *follower* trotting behind, then another, then fifty. Where are they all coming **from**? **From** the sea, **from** the palm trees, **from** under the stair carpet. The tsar demands to know where they are **from**, and they all point back at him.

The {Shepherd} sits in the {Basement} of the {Stadium} under a *lookout* tower, his *heart* thumping, trying hard **to think**. He **thinks** so hard that steam rises from his ears. The steam floats up to the lookout and forms a cloud shaped like an idea, and the crowd above gasps: they can all see what he **thinks**.

The {Sheriff} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Beehive} to inspect a bee with a towering *hairdo* that scrapes the *roof*. 'Is that hair **real**?' He tugs it and the bee yelps. It's **real**! The other bees gasp, then line the stairs combing their fuzz, desperate to grow **real** hair too.

The {Robot} bursts up through the {Trapdoor} of the {Beehive} carrying the *sun* in its claws like a hot pizza. Honey melts, wax drips, bees put on tiny sunglasses. The **sun** is too hot to hold, so the robot juggles it, beeping in alarm, and finally hangs the **sun** back in the sky, slightly dented.

The {Juggler} stands on the {Rooftop} of the {Dunes} watchtower as an *army* of camels marches across the sand. She tosses up a ball, and the whole **army** stops to watch. She juggles ten, and the **army** cheers, drops its spears and joins in, until a thousand soldiers are juggling their way across the desert.

The {Jockey} peeks into the {Basement} of the {Hut} and finds a *busy man* wearing a badge for every job: **one who** cooks, **one who** sweeps, **one who** sings to the potatoes. He dashes from task to task so fast he blurs. The jockey pins on a badge of her own: **one who** watches.

The {Yogi} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Beach} bar, where *music* plays straight into his *heart*. Every note carries a hidden **meaning**: the drum says hello, the flute says lunch, the trumpet says your trousers are on fire. The yogi leaps into the sea, finally understanding the true **meaning** of jazz.

The {Wizard} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Pool} slide behind a *vanishing man* who fades away bit by bit. First he is **without** his hat, then **without** his legs, then **without** his head. Only his swimming trunks whoosh down the slide, **without** anybody in them, and land in the water with a splash.

The {Lifeguard} bursts out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Beach} tower flexing one *strong arm*. With pure **power** she lifts a capsized boat, tosses a whale back to sea and arm-wrestles the tide until the waves give up. The seagulls bow. Every swimmer feels the **power** and paddles very politely.

The {Tailor} is sewing on the {Rooftop} of the {Spa} when a long *serpent* slithers up. Nobody knows what **it** is. **It** eats a towel. **It** wraps itself round the chimney. **It** steals her measuring tape and measures itself: forty metres. Everyone just calls **it** It, because no one dares to ask.

The {Yogi} finds a *gift* in the {Basement} of the {Museum} and unwraps it: a sock **and** a teapot **and** a goldfish **and** a trumpet. Every layer of paper reveals another **and**. He keeps unwrapping until the basement is knee deep in paper, **and** the curator comes down asking who ordered the camel.

The {Chef} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Hangar} trailing *long hair* behind her, so **long** it spills down every step, across the floor and out onto the runway. A plane taxis over it. Mechanics use it as a tow rope. She tries to plait it, but it keeps growing **longer**, all the way to the next airport.

The {Baker} slips into the {Basement} of the {Spa}, where a *python* is stealing the cupcakes. A *helping hand* shoots out of the wall **to hold** the snake by its tail. Then it **holds** the cupcakes, **holds** the baker's hat, **holds** the door, until it is **holding** everything and nothing in the room can move.

The {Juggler} builds a **machine** on the {Rooftop} of the {Beach} café out of a *tree* and a *small table*. She pulls a lever: the tree shakes coconuts onto the table, which flips them into the air for her to catch. The **machine** speeds up, coconuts flying everywhere, until it starts juggling the juggler too.

The {Sheriff} paints a big *cross* on each step of the {Staircase} of the {Beehive}, counting aloud all the way to **ten**. On each cross a bee stands guard: **ten** steps, **ten** crosses, **ten** bees. An eleventh bee tries to squeeze in, and the sheriff sends it home with a ticket: only **ten** allowed.

The {Magician} on the {Staircase} of the {Inn} pulls a *commoner* out of his hat, then another, then two hundred. The **people** pour down the stairs into the bar, ordering soup, singing, demanding a vote. He tries to stuff the **people** back in, but they have already elected the innkeeper's dog as mayor.

The {Dentist} pops out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Beach} lifeguard tower with a *slingshot* made of *bamboo* and fires coconuts at a row of crabs. A scoreboard ranks every catch: **number** one, **number** two, **number** three. Each crab gets a rosette saying first, second or third, and the last one sulks in a shell.

The {Gardener} plants a whole *town square* on the {Rooftop} of the {Lagoon} hotel: fountain, benches, pigeons. A sign says **public**, everyone welcome. Dolphins leap up to sit on the benches, tourists picnic, a brass band moves in. The manager complains, but it's **public** now, and nobody is allowed to lock it.

The {Tsar} storms into the {Basement} of the {Beehive}, stamps his boot down on *this spot* and declares, '**This**! Right here, **this**!' He builds a throne on it. The bees bring him honey, but only on **this** exact spot; one step to the left and they ignore him completely.

The {Yogi} rushes down to the {Basement} of the {Beach} house to start the party, but it has **already** happened. The cake is **already** eaten, the balloons **already** popped, the guests **already** asleep in hammocks. Even the washing-up is **already** done. The yogi sighs and lies down, **already** late for tomorrow.

The {Gardener} drags a *workbench* onto the {Rooftop} of the {Lagoon} lighthouse and starts to **work**: sawing, hammering, gluing. In an hour she builds a boat, a bridge and a robot duck. The duck immediately gets to **work** too, and soon the roof is a clattering factory of ducks building more ducks.

The {Sheriff} marches into the {Basement} of the {Beehive}, where a *clerk* is bossing around a *standing person*. 'I'll **make** you dance!' The person dances. 'I'll **make** you sing!' He sings. The sheriff grabs the clerk's pen, and now he **makes** the clerk dance instead while the bees hum along.

The {Cheerleader} runs up the {Staircase} of the {Boxing Ring} hugging a *standing heart* covered in green *moss*. Every time it beats, a new **feeling** washes over the crowd: joy, gloom, a sudden urge for sandwiches. The boxers hug and sob. The referee writes poems. Nobody can fight with this much **feeling**.

The {Magician} on the {Staircase} of the {Boxing Ring} pulls the *sun and moon* from his hat and hangs them both above the ring. It is so **bright** that the boxers wear three pairs of sunglasses. The crowd glows, popcorn pops in the heat, and even the shadows flee, because everywhere is far too **bright**.

The {Shepherd} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Boxing Ring} and plants a *seedling* beside a *standing heart*. However hard the boxers punch it, the seedling just grows; that is its **nature**. The heart beats calmly; its **nature** is gentle. By the final bell a forest fills the ring, and the boxers are napping in it.

The {Jockey} climbs onto the {Rooftop} of the {Beehive} to visit a *sage* who **knows** everything. 'Which horse will win?' He **knows**. 'Where are my keys?' He **knows**. 'How many bees live here?' He **knows** that too, and counts them out loud, all fifty thousand, until the jockey falls asleep.

The {Cheerleader} drags a *treasure chest* up the {Staircase} of the {Mint} and tips out every coin ever made. 'The **whole** lot!' she cheers, then balances a **whole** gold bar on her nose. The guards give chase, and she tumbles down the **whole** staircase inside the chest, clanking like a drum kit.

The {Sailor} nails *three planks* to the {Rooftop} of the {Mansion} to build a raft. On it she loads **three** parrots, **three** barrels and **three** cannons. A storm floods the mansion, the raft floats free, and she sails round and round the garden to **three** loud cheers from the butler.

The {Yogi} falls through the {Trapdoor} of the {Boathouse}, climbs out, and falls in **again**. His *right hand* waves from the water. He climbs out, slips on a fish, and splashes in **again**. By the tenth time the ducks are holding up score cards and quacking '**Again**! **Again**!'

The {Gardener} stands on the {Rooftop} of the {Swan Pond} pavilion guarding a tiny *mountain pass* made of flowerpots. When the swans try to march through, she slams the gate: **closed**! Then she **closes** the windows, **closes** the umbrellas and **closes** her eyes. The swans peck at the gate and waddle off to sulk.

The {Dentist} visits a *fortune teller* in the {Basement} of the {Yen Exchange}, who flicks glowing *embers* onto a map. Each one lands as a tiny burning **dot**. 'Your future,' she whispers, joining the **dots** with a pencil: a picture of a toothbrush. The dentist sighs and adds one more **dot** for a smile.

The {Jockey} gallops out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Jungle} lodge towards a *goal line* painted between two trees. She rides **straight**: no bends, no zigzags, **straight** through vines, **straight** through a waterfall, past a baffled tiger. She crosses the line leaving a perfectly **straight** stripe of flattened leaves.

The {Yogi} pops out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Hut} and builds a *scaffold* round it to open a **business**: yoga classes on every level. Customers climb up, stretch and pay in bananas. The **business** booms, the scaffold sways, and soon the yogi has an office, a tie and a hundred employees doing headstands.

The {Wizard} climbs out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Island} cabin under a *dusk moon*, shaking a *fortune stick*. It jumps from the cup and points **outside**: the party is out there! Music and fireworks all happen **outside**, on the sand. He tries to go back in, but even the furniture has moved **outside**.

The {Juggler} on the {Rooftop} of the {Stadium} performs for a *general* who announces the future. 'You **will** drop that ball.' She drops it. 'You **will** sneeze.' She sneezes. 'The crowd **will** do the wave.' Ninety thousand people stand up. Whatever the general says **will** happen, happens.

The {Lifeguard} weighs everything on a *balance scale* in the {Basement} of the {Stadium}. Every time she puts something in one pan, a twin pops up in the other. **Two** footballs, **two** goalkeepers, **two** mascots in identical chicken suits. She blows her whistle in alarm and hears **two** whistles back.

The {Gardener} on the {Rooftop} of the {Tower} waters her sunflowers, and the whole *tower* grows with them. Each splash adds another floor. **Tall**, **taller**, so **tall** that clouds snag on her hat and geese stop to ask for directions. She waves to an aeroplane passing far beneath her boots.

The {Juggler} on the {Rooftop} of the {Yen Exchange} juggles coins across the *gap* **between** two buildings. Each coin flies **between** her hands and the neighbour's window. One drops into the gap, so she wedges herself **between** the walls to fetch it, and gets stuck **between** two grumpy pigeons.

The {Yogi} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Boathouse} and finds a *sprouting field* growing on every step. Everything springs **from** it: carrots, rowing boats, a confused goose. 'Where did you come **from**?' he asks the goose. It points down at the soil: **from** here, like everything else.

The {Wizard} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Funfair} and finds a *gate* with a giant *mouth* in the middle. It won't open until it **asks** a riddle: 'What is a duck's favourite ride?' The wizard has no idea. The mouth keeps **asking**, so the wizard **asks** one back, and they're still at it at closing time.

The {Hunter} creeps into the {Basement} of the {Funfair} following muddy *footsteps*, and meets a *glare* so fierce it melts his torch. He is **very** scared. **Very**, **very** scared. The glare belongs to a goldfish in a plastic bag, who is **very** angry about losing at hoopla.

The {Zookeeper} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Waiting Room}, where a *grabbing hand* snatches the *sun* off a poster: whoever grabs the **most** wins it. Everyone scrambles: the **most** magazines, the **most** chairs, the **most** biscuits. The zookeeper wins, holding the **most**, buried up to her chin in leaflets.

The {Jockey} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Lagoon} pier holding a *heavy weight*, so **heavy** that she sinks straight to the bottom. Fish try to lift it and fail. A whale tries and groans. So she rides it like a horse along the seabed, one **heavy** step at a time, until she bumps into a shipwreck.

The {Baker} pops out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Boxing Ring} on a toy train running along *linked rails*. He delivers a loaf, **and also** a pie, **and also** a cake shaped like the referee. The boxers stop fighting to eat, **and also** to dance, **and also** to beg him for the recipe.

The {Wizard} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Pool} and casts a spell that turns every **thing** into a *cow*. Beach balls, flip-flops, the diving board: all cows, each waving a little *pennant* with its old name. One pennant just says THING, because nobody remembers what that **thing** used to be.

The {Sheriff} climbs into the {Basement} of the {Boathouse}, and a giant *hand* rises out of the water to shake his. It squeezes so hard his hat flies off. The **hand** waves, gives a thumbs up, then plays rock, paper, scissors with him and wins every time. The sheriff raises his own **hand** in surrender.

The {Yogi} sits on the {Rooftop} of the {Boxing Ring} in a little *shed* full of rules. Whenever a boxer looks up, he shouts through the window: 'You **should** stretch! You **should** breathe! You **should** hug, not punch!' The boxers feel guilty, do what they **should**, and the fight turns into a yoga class.

The {Jockey} bursts out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Mansion} to find a *fortune teller* swinging a *halberd* at the butler. They **fight** over the last biscuit, crashing through vases and chandeliers. The jockey rides between them yelling 'No **fighting**!' but they keep **fighting** until the biscuit crumbles to dust.

The {Shepherd} climbs out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Stadium} with a giant *weathervane* strapped to his hat. Wherever it spins, everything rushes **towards** it: sheep run **towards** it, footballs roll **towards** it, ninety thousand fans lean **towards** it. He spins round once, and the whole stadium tips sideways.

The {Tailor} on the {Staircase} of the {Boathouse} sews a giant *hairdo* onto a customer's **head**: braids, ribbons, a small rowing boat. It is so big that the **head** won't fit through the door. The customer has to crawl down the stairs **head** first while seagulls build a nest in the bun.

The {Wizard} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Funfair} with a new *tattoo* that keeps turning into **writing**: poems, shopping lists, a letter to his gran. Visitors queue to read it. The **writing** spreads off his arm onto the ride cars and the candyfloss, until the whole fair is one long, wiggling story.

The {Tailor} in the {Basement} of the {Beach} house measures a *standing person* whose feet have grown *roots* into the floor. She measures his whole **body**: arms, legs, belly, ears. The **body** won't budge, so she sews the suit right onto him and leaves him standing there like a very well-dressed tree.

The {Jockey} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Jungle} parliament, where monkeys argue across a *goal line* painted on the floor. A tortoise bangs a *cane* for order. This is **politics**: shouting, voting, throwing bananas. The jockey is elected leader by accident and has to do **politics** all afternoon.
